result:
I reviewed this against `SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md` and rejected it. Key finding: this task's own diff is documentation-only — the real code fix (commit `77de705`, punch-list PATCH gate + `PATCH /api/org-members/[id]` role-assignment endpoint) was pushed directly to a *different, independently-dispatched task's* branch (`worker/task-20260727-122935-...`, confirmed as PR #53's actual head via `gh pr view`), not this task's own isolated worktree — a direct violation of the dispatch model's own-worktree/no-collision rule. There's also an apparent duplicate task branch (`...-130236`) with the same title and zero commits, suggesting the pre-dispatch duplicate-scope check was skipped.

I went and read the actual fix on the foreign branch to review it properly regardless: the two security fixes themselves are sound (punch-list PATCH now gates identically to its sibling POST; the new role-assignment endpoint is correctly gated and tested), but it has one real untested gap — no protection against demoting an org's last owner/admin, which could re-create the same lockout class this change was meant to fix. Full reasoning and all issues are in `review-verdict.json`.
